- The MSD fit window moves D_3D(Li) at 500 K from 0.0298 to 0.0309 Å²/ps (about 3%), so Ea is not sensitive to it. The `fit_range` option through the `msd` verb returned identical values, so I checked the fit directly with numpy.

**Diffusion coefficients (cm²/s)**

| T (K) | D in-plane (2D) | D 3D (Einstein, slope/6) |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 4.63e-6 | 3.09e-6 |
| 600 | 1.78e-5 | 1.18e-5 |
| 700 | 3.56e-5 | 2.37e-5 |
| 800 | 5.20e-5 | 3.47e-5 |
| 900 | 8.55e-5 | 5.70e-5 |

The 3D Einstein value understates the transport because the motion is 2D. I report the in-plane D as the main value; the 3D value is 2/3 of it, and both give the same Ea.

**Paragraph for the results section**

Li transport was studied by VASP molecular dynamics in the NVT ensemble (2 fs time step, 10 ps per run) at 500, 600, 700, 800 and 900 K, using a 128-atom Li₆₄S₆₄ cell (a = 16 Å). The Li mean-squared displacement grows linearly in x and y, while its z component stays near zero (|D_z| ≤ 5×10⁻⁵ Å²/ps at all temperatures), so Li diffuses in-plane. The in-plane diffusivity, D = (D_x + D_y)/2, is 4.6×10⁻⁶ cm²/s at 500 K, 1.8×10⁻⁵ cm²/s at 600 K, 3.6×10⁻⁵ cm²/s at 700 K, 5.2×10⁻⁵ cm²/s at 800 K and 8.5×10⁻⁵ cm²/s at 900 K. An Arrhenius fit of ln D against 1/T (r² = 0.988) gives an activation energy of 0.275 ± 0.017 eV and a prefactor of 3.1×10⁻³ cm²/s. The sulfur sublattice shows no measurable diffusion.
